On-Page SEO Basics: Titles, Meta Tags, and Clean Structure

September 1, 2026 by Dana Lee

Search optimization starts on the page itself: the head metadata, the body structure, and the structured data a crawler reads before it renders anything. This guide answers the question directly: fix the head first, keep one topic per page, and let the markup describe the content.

Write the head metadata

The charset declaration comes first so the parser never guesses an encoding. The viewport meta makes the page usable on phones, the title names the topic, and the description summarizes the promise of the page in one or two sentences. A canonical link tells crawlers which URL owns the content.

In a 2026 reader survey, 47% of respondents said they rewrite the title last, after the body copy is final. reader survey

Structure the page semantically

One main landmark, one h1, and headings that step down without skipping levels give both readers and crawlers a clean outline. Wrap the primary content in an article, put captions under figures, and give dates a time element with a machine-readable datetime attribute.

Ship structured data that machines trust

A single JSON-LD block with a schema.org graph links the organization, the website, the page, the article, and its breadcrumb trail. Every URL is absolute, every date is ISO 8601, and the article headline matches the visible h1, so the markup and the page tell the same story.
